‘AGEs are thought to contribute to microvascular disease and to
the accelerated atherosclerosis observed in patients with dia
betes (1,3). To better characterize the basis ofthe interaction of
AGEs with ther cellular targets, cll surface-associated AGE,
binding proteins have been isolated (4,6). Our laboratory has
purified, cloned, and expressed an integral membrane protein
which is a new member ofthe immunoglebulin superfamily of
cell surface molecules and binds AGE ligands in a manner
similar to intact endothelial cells (ECs) and monocytes (this
receptor is termod Receptor for AGE = RAGE) (6-1) A second
AGE binding protein was purified from tistue extracts which
‘was closely related to the iron binding protein lactoferrin (LF),
‘based on identity of the amino-terminal sequences, cross-reac:
tivity of the respective antisera, identical mobility on SDS-
PAGE, and similar binding of AGE ligands (the latter was
termed the lactoferrin-ike AGE binding protein or LP-L) (8)
Furthermore, molecular cloning studies of LI-L using probes
based on the protein sequence at the amino terminus and of
internal tryptic peptides of LY-L resulted in the cloning of a
«DNA identical with bovine LF (6, 9; this has been deposited in
GenBank; Accession No. L06604). Thus, LF and LF-L would
appear to be virtually identical, although distinct from RAGE.
Although RAGE and LP-L each bound AGE ligands alone, plot
studies suggested that the two molecules were associated on
the EC and monocyte surface (5, 7). Ths led us to undertake
the current experiments with the goal of characterizing the
interaction of RAGE and LF-L,
